metadata.case_name: LUI SHEUNG LOK v. WAH WAH TRAVEL SERVICES LTD.

source: On the day of the accident, the plaintiff was admitted with severe burns to his head, neck and both upper limbs involving 15% of his body surface.

injuries.description: Severe burns to neck with burn scar contracture
source: On the day of the accident, the plaintiff was admitted with severe burns to his head, neck and both upper limbs involving 15% of his body surface.

In January of the following year, pressure garment therapy followed in an attempt to control excessive scarring. He had to wear pressure garments on his right arm until May 1998 and on his neck until March 1998.
On 23 April 1997, he was re-admitted to hospital for Z plasty operation for burn scar contracture of the neck.

injuries.description: Severe burns to both upper limbs with residual weakness and reduced dexterity of right arm and hand; infected wound on right arm
injuries.body_part: both upper limbs (right arm and hand notable)
source: On the day of the accident, the plaintiff was admitted with severe burns to his head, neck and both upper limbs involving 15% of his body surface.
His wounds were debrided and dressed. Two painful skin graft operations were conducted in November 1996.
He was re-admitted on 6 December 1996 for debridement of an infected wound on his right arm.
Four years on and the plaintiff still has extensive scars on his neck, right arm and hand and right leg, a constant source of itching, discomfort and embarrassment to him.
His right arm and hand are weak as flexibility has been significantly reduced.
